Source and attribution

The archive attributes this English wording to Self-Reliance and files it under Transcendentalism. That locator distinguishes the passage from loose internet attributions: readers can return to the named work or section to check translation, surrounding argument, and edition-specific wording.

About Ralph Waldo Emerson

Ralph Waldo Emerson (1803–1882) was the American Transcendentalist essayist and lecturer who urged self-reliance and unbroken relation to nature and the Over-Soul. A former Unitarian minister in Concord, he gathered the Dial circle and mentored younger writers including Thoreau.

How to read this passage

Across 4 recurring voices here (notably Søren Kierkegaard and Ralph Waldo Emerson), authenticity is framed through Transcendentalism and Existentialism. Some passages define authenticity; others warn how it fails; still others relocate it inside habit, community, or language. This passage enters that discussion through authenticity, growth, courage.

Concepts in this quote

Authenticity
Authenticity appears in this archive as a live philosophical concern—not a slogan. These verified English passages show how thinkers treat authenticity as a problem of judgment, practice, or explanation.
Growth
Growth appears in this archive as a live philosophical concern—not a slogan. These verified English passages show how thinkers treat growth as a problem of judgment, practice, or explanation.
Courage
Courage is the virtue of facing fear without abandoning judgment—central to ethics from Aristotle to modern existential resolve.
